site_class.value: mid-latitude with shallow ground ice (Arcadia Planitia class)
site_class.basis: Q-022: profile input; equatorial (more sunlight, less accessible ice) is the alternative value.

surplus_outlets.value: in-situ store and production down-rate; no export boundary
surplus_outlets.basis: Q-026: where export is impractical, the surplus stores in-situ or production down-rates; the locale profile states the outlet set.

planetary_protection.value: sited outside COSPAR special regions; the parcel check is a site design step
planetary_protection.basis: Q-027: ground ice may lie in a special region under the COSPAR policy.

crew.basis: Q-029: crew size is a profile entry derived from the locale habitable volume and food production; 4 is the issued HAB design occupancy. A locale profile may set its own.

g_m_s2.note: partial gravity: settling, flotation and packed columns work but more slowly

pressure_Pa.verification_test: In-situ pressure measurement at the landing site

breathable.note: CO2 atmosphere with trace O2; pressurised shells required

vent_sink.note: nothing vents to an atmosphere that cannot take it; vents go to recovery

oxidant.note: no usable oxygen; combustion requires plant oxygen

shell_pressure_kPa.note: pressurised shells hold a sea-level-equivalent interior; process and relief physics see this space, not the external atmosphere

pv_yield_kWh_kWp_d.verification_test: Solar geometry with optical-depth and dust-settling losses
pv_yield_kWh_kWp_d.note: Mars mean 586.2 W/m2 before dust-settling losses (NASA_MARS_FACT)

night_hours.note: Mars sol 24.66 h; night approximately half the sol (NASA_MARS_FACT)

dust_stretch_d.verification_test: In-situ optical-depth record through one dust season at the landing site, backed by an orbital opacity survey
dust_stretch_d.note: Design-basis dust season: the 2018 planet-encircling dust event held surface PV to a small fraction of clear-sol output for about three months (orbital colour-imager record, June-August 2018, full decay through September). The dust-season energy figures in power_portfolio.dust_stretch_design scale linearly with this duration.

basic_wind_speed_m_s.verification_test: Metocean model at the landing site

snow.not_applicable: No snow; the atmosphere is too thin for precipitation

SDS_g.units: g (marsquakes recorded by InSight are small)

dose_rate_mSv_d.units: mSv/d dose equivalent at Gale crater
dose_rate_mSv_d.note: regolith cover and water shielding reduce the habitable-space dose

value.note: the worst stretch is the sol night plus a dust storm

value.study: F-20261113-01 mars surface-power design study, complete; the mix enters power_portfolio.sources as designed sources under the Q-024 revision (2026-11-15); the installed counts solve in flow_graph/param/site_units.py from the portfolio balance and the backup_fuel critical list

load_book.register: graph demand at the base plate (mvs.electrical.need_kw less the EXT_HALL roof extension, which a non-roof locale does not build); AQS-PLAN-011 section 5.5 worst-stretch balance; backup_fuel critical list (AQS-ELEC-007)

roof_verdict.verdict: PV-only cannot close at any footprint: the need at the base plate is 75 x the base-plate roof, and the extension envelope load at the minus 89 C heating design grows the demand faster than the array grows the roof (best gap on the whole bay-grid growth range minus 658 kWp)
roof_verdict.register: solver.roof_close bay-grid scan at the mars profile

fission.kind: surface fission, NASA Fission Surface Power class, uranium fueled (Kilopower heritage)
fission.basis: NASA Fission Surface Power 40 kW electric-class unit; the study booked the PV-only-balance dust deficit 67.8 kW / 40 kW per unit = 1.69 -> 2 duty units plus one installed spare (N+1), at PV share 1.0. The fission carrier is dust-blind: it delivers 100 percent through the stretch
fission.status: designed source (study F-20261113-01 complete; Q-024 revision 2026-11-15); the installed count solves in flow_graph/param/site_units.py at the issued mix shares and is stamped on the FSP_40K graph node

rtg.kind: radioisotope thermoelectric generator, NASA MMRTG class (general-purpose heat source)
rtg.basis: MMRTG-class 110 W electric at beginning of mission; sized on the 2.0 kW controls-and-instruments slice of the critical list: 2000 W / 110 W = 18.2 -> 19 units at 2.09 kW electric, the extreme-reliability trickle that keeps controls alive through a loss of both PV and fission. The full 14.6 kW critical list on RTGs would need 133 units and is rejected as incommensurate; kilowatt-class criticals stay on the fission base with the fuel cell and battery as the diverse backups (AQS-ELEC-007)
rtg.status: designed source (study F-20261113-01 complete; Q-024 revision 2026-11-15); the count solves in flow_graph/param/site_units.py from the backup_fuel critical list and is stamped on the MMRTG graph node

dust_season_store.verdict: a PV-only dust-season store is rejected: 198.4 MWh is 156 x the night bank the locale books and needs 66 clear sols of the whole clear-sol surplus to charge before the storm
dust_season_store.with_fission_base: the night bank stays as built: ZNBR2 1273 kWh at the locale demand, night coverage 4.76; the fission base carries the 91.9 kW dust deficit, and the mix leaves a 60.8 MWh surplus over the 90 d season

dust_stretch_design.basis: Sized from the profile load book on published bases: NASA Fission Surface Power (40 kW electric class), NASA MMRTG (110 W electric class), NASA_MARS_FACT (2018 global dust storm, dust-stretch duration in solar.dust_stretch_d). The dedicated reference keys register with the graph units when the study closes (Q-024).
